items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Harry White said... 'Charlie Johnson. All them boys who were banjo players, they’re playing guitars.' ... 'There was Charlie Johnson at Smalls’ Paradise.'

ctx.x: In Harlem. It’s a club on 133rd Street. Later it became Dickie Wells’s nightclub. It was on a basement on the ground floor with a club called the . . . a funny name. The Fun Box? No. The Fun Box is near . . . The Mad House, on the first floor. The Mad

House. Downstairs was the Nest Club. I played in there. You go to work at ten o’clock at night and you come out ten o’clock in the morning, because it was a depression that set in, and we didn’t get a crowd until after three o’clock in the morning. Three, four, five . . . five o’clock, the band go on, because you sit there all night. There might be parties drifting in. It was just to winter. I had never seen snow, real snow falling. The doorman there, he had seven singers there: Mamie Smith, Clara Smith, and…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Him and Jimmy Harrison... They were in Charlie Johnson's band

ctx.x: And In New York... He cut everybody in New York. Everybody who thought they could play a trumpet ain't messin'... Him and Jimmy Harrison, they were the two, trombone and trumpet... They were in Charlie Johnson's band, and they're speaking(?) to him, and then Sidney DeParis, and them three... Fletcher Henderson's band didn't have nothin' on Charlie Johnson's band. But Charlie Johnson was working at Small's Paradise, and the difference was that Fletcher was down at the Roseland Ballroom. But them people was out of…
Yeah, I heard about it. I missed him. I didn't get to hear him. What about Big Green, too? Because I hear so much about him. Did you hear him?
